title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
why_read: A clever and rigorous benchmark testing LLM navigation and reasoning via the Wikipedia Game, offering real comparative data across languages and model types.
analysis: The researchers use the Wikipedia Game — navigating from one article to a target using only hyperlinks — as a controlled testbed for evaluating how well language models can do multi-step, graph-based information retrieval using semantic cues. They compare embedding models and LLMs like GPT-4o, GPT-o3 mini, and DeepSeek-R1 against human performance and TF-IDF baselines, across five languages and five academic datasets. The finding that no model clearly beats humans, and that rankings vary heavily by language and topic, is a useful and sobering data point for anyone deploying LLMs for retrieval tasks. The methodology, building large local Wikipedia and citation graphs via OpenAlex without needing third-party APIs, is also a reusable technical contribution.
